chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Hot Chocolates and Connie's Inn: the shows and Louis's jealousy
summary: Zutty played in pit bands, not as soloist; Louis did the Broadway show then returned to Connie's Inn, singing Black and Blue. Marge says friends believed Louis was jealous of Zutty's popularity with the show girls.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Zutty in these shows like Hot Chocolates, were you featured as a soloist?
No. They just wanted me to play in the pit bands.
So in other words when Louis was there in Hot Chocolates, there was no question of you stealing the limelight from him in any way?

No, no, but he wouldn't let them bring me down to play the Broadway show, he wanted me to stay in Connie's Inn to take care of the band. One of those things. You know what I mean? Because they wanted me, because Leonard Harper had spoke to me about playing this show on Broadway.
Well when you said the show on Broadway, Louis didn't go to the show on Broadway?
He was in the show on Broadway. He was in Connie's Inn, play the show and then come back to Connie's Inn.
Oh then you had to, you had to stay at Connie's Inn?
Yes that's when he sang that 'Black and Blue' and all that stuff.

But personally there was a little jealousy in those days with Louis. And that's what Barney (Bonnie?) says all the time, Louis was jealous you know. And Pop Foster says the same thing. And EARVELL SHAW says the same thing you know and all. But the show girls, the dancing girls, the acts the hits, they loved Zuddy so, you know. They wanted, they hadn't had anybody they said to play like that for them. And I think that made Louis feel like Zuddy was ...........
Oh, you mean he was very popular with the people in the show?
People in the show and all you know.
But Zuddy didn't have no band.
